layers.title: CPRA project footprints
layers.attribution: Louisiana CPRA — attribution wording pending confirmation (see data/gis/sources.json openQuestions.cpra-cims-terms-of-use)
layers.description: CPRA coastal protection and restoration project footprints (statewide service, shown here within Iberia Parish only). Note: this is a joined ArcGIS view — its own field names carry table-qualified prefixes (e.g. "Project_Status_List.Project_Name"), a real service quirk left to the engine's default "show all fields with aliases" popup fallback rather than a guessed exact-name mapping.

layers.title: CPRA projects (Iberia Parish)
layers.attribution: Louisiana CPRA — attribution wording pending confirmation (see data/gis/sources.json openQuestions.cpra-cims-terms-of-use)
layers.description: CPRA project center points (public 'CPRA Projects (Center Points)' service, AGOL item 20422ab8cbce407a8970d2fc549272ae), filtered server-side to Iberia Parish via the where clause above. Distinct from the cpra-projects layer above, which is a different, statewide polygon-footprints service (CPRA_Polys, no Parish field, can't be attribute-filtered) -- this layer is point geometry and is what a per-project guided tour (see data/gis/featuretours/) attaches to. Same joined-view field-prefixing quirk as cpra-projects (Project_Status_List.*), and this service reports no objectIdField/globalIdField at all -- Project_Status_List.Project_ID (CPRA's own stable business key, e.g. "TV-0031") is used for feature identity here, not an ArcGIS OBJECTID. Known limitation, not chased further: the Filter tool's setWhere() replaces this layer's where entirely rather than ANDing with it, so a visitor using Filter on this specific layer could temporarily see non-Iberia projects until the filter is cleared or the map reloads. zIndex is deliberately 95, not the ~20 a 'coastal' group layer would otherwise get: parish-boundary (zIndex 90, always visible, a filled -- if nearly-transparent -- interactive polygon covering the whole parish) sits on its own canvas pane under this map's preferCanvas engine, and Leaflet's canvas click dispatch only ever tests the topmost pane's shapes -- a miss there does not fall through to lower panes. Below 90, this layer's pins would never receive a click at all. Do not lower this back into the group's normal z-order without addressing that click-routing behavior first (see js/gis/gis-viewer.js's buildParishMask() comment for the same issue on the dim mask, fixed via pointer-events, and the CHANGES.md entry documenting this as a broader, not-yet-fixed limitation for every other layer below parish-boundary).
